_comment: SYNTHETIC — hand-built from the documented response shapes in Yahoo's official
Fantasy Sports API guide and from published wrapper-library samples (yfpy,
yahoo_fantasy_api). NOT a live capture. Yahoo API access is gated behind an
approval application and NO live call has ever been made from this repo.
Replace with a real redacted capture once API access is approved.
AUTHORED 2026-08-11 (not captured on any date). The 32 player resources were
hand-authored and then serialized by a throwaway script so that every one of
them has the identical field ORDER and nesting — a hand-typed 25-entry page
would eventually contain a typo that looked exactly like a parser bug.
REDACTION: league and team identifiers are invented; headshot URLs are fake
(FAKEHEADSHOT<id>). Player names are real NFL players — public sports data,
not personal data of any league member — and their numeric ids are PLAUSIBLE
BUT UNVERIFIED. No token, email or real GUID appears anywhere here.
MODELS: GET /fantasy/v2/league/461.l.576919/players;start=0;count=25?format=json
WHY THIS IS COMMITTED — THIS IS THE FULL PAGE, AND 'FULL' IS THE SIGNAL.
It holds EXACTLY 25 players, and 25 is not a number anyone chose: Yahoo hard
-caps every page of the players collection at 25 items no matter what count
you ask for, and that cap is UNDOCUMENTED. A full page therefore means
'there is probably more' and pagination MUST continue; the short page in
yahoo_players_page2.json is what says stop.
Why the pair matters more than either file: a league's player universe is
1,000+ players, i.e. 40+ requests per league-season against a per-client_id
rate limit. Stopping early looks EXACTLY like success — you get players,
they parse, the rows are real. Nothing raises. The only defence is the page
-length rule these two fixtures encode, plus the provider's own 'count'
which parse_players_collection() returns alongside the rows precisely so a
caller can compare declared against parsed and notice a short read.
SHAPE HAZARDS DELIBERATELY PRESENT:
1. 'players' is a numeric-key COLLECTION with a sibling 'count' of 25.
Keys "10"-"24" sort BEFORE "2" lexically; iter_collection() sorts them
numerically.
2. Each 'player' is an ARRAY whose only element is an ARRAY of single-key
dicts, one per field. Two levels of nesting before the first scalar.
3. index 17 (Ashton Jeanty) has NO editorial_player_key. player_uid must
fall back to the bare player_id and rebuild 'nfl.p.41011' from the
season-INDEPENDENT game code — never from the season's game id, or the
same human becomes a new player every year and all cross-season history
silently splits in two.
4. eligible_positions is a numeric list for flex-eligible skill players
and a BARE OBJECT for QB/K/DEF — the single-element collapse.
5. Names carry a typographic apostrophe (Ja’Marr, De’Von) in the display
fields and a plain one in the ascii fields; one name carries a period
and a hyphen (Amon-Ra St. Brown); one carries a generational suffix
(Brian Thomas Jr.). normalize_name() strips all of it — for FALLBACK
MATCHING ONLY. Two different players can normalize to the same string,
so a name-only match that writes a crosswalk row merges two careers.
6. Injury fields appear on two players only, and are ABSENT (not empty) on
the healthy ones.
7. The team defense has no uniform_number and an empty last name.
NOT TRUNCATED — the count of 25 IS the fixture. Do not add or remove a
player without changing 'count' to match, or the file starts asserting
something it does not mean.
